From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medix.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Medix AI Security <compliance@medix.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Privacy intake: DPA + telemetry ingest boundary for Medix pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for agreeing to run the pilot with Medix. As part of our security review we need a few clarifications tied to the DPA and how Redwood will handle telemetry/ingest data from our integration. We are specifically focused on PII handling and evidence we can attach to our vendor review. Our asks: 

- Ingest boundary manifest: list of fields Redwood will see in the ingestion path for our connector and which of those you consider PII / sensitive (PII definitions below).
- Telemetry segmentation: how is telemetry separated from customer content? What telemetry is retained for debugging vs product analytics? Retention tiers.
- KMS and key custody: describe who holds keys (Redwood KMS, customer KMS, HSM options) and an attestation sample for key custody model.
- Subprocessor roster for any components involved in ingest (CDN, observability, backup/archive).
- Cross-border transfers: any non-US egress processing, and legal basis / SCCs used.
- Evidence: a labeled dataflow diagram (ingest -> proxy -> runtime -> logs/telemetry stores) and SOC 2 control mappings for ingestion.

I've attached our short SSQ (SSQ-Medix-20251004.pdf) with fine-grained questions — would appreciate a response by next Thursday (10/9) so our procurement and legal teams can complete the review. If it helps we can do a 30-min call mid-week.

PII note: our definition includes name, email, phone, national identifiers, medical metadata, and any health-related free-text that could be linked to a patient.

Thanks,

Sarah Liu
Head of Security
Medix AI

Attachment: SSQ-Medix-20251004.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medix.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Oct 2025 at 09:12 AM
Subject: Privacy intake: DPA + telemetry ingest boundary for Medix pilot

> - Ingest boundary manifest: list of fields Redwood will see in the ingestion path for our connector and which of those you consider PII / sensitive (PII definitions below).

Draft answer (short): Redwood's ingest path accepts customer-provided payloads via a TLS-protected connector endpoint. Fields commonly seen: user_id, email, display_name, message_text, metadata.platform, metadata.device_id, timestamps, and application-specific payloads. We classify the following as PII by default: email, display_name (if linked), national identifiers, phone numbers, and any medical identifiers / flagged health text. Non-PII telemetry (for debugging) includes anonymized error hashes, stack traces with no identifiers, latency metrics, and sampling of aggregated model telemetry.

> - Telemetry segmentation: how is telemetry separated from customer content? What telemetry is retained for debugging vs product analytics? Retention tiers.

Draft answer (short): We separate content and telemetry at the ingestion proxy. Content flows to the runtime KV/cache and ephemeral logs; telemetry is copied to a separate observability pipeline (ingest-traces, metrics, anonymized logs). Retention tiers: ephemeral debugging logs (7 days), anonymized traces (90 days), aggregated analytics (3 years). We provide controls to customers to opt-out of non-essential telemetry and to request deletion of sampled logs.

> - KMS and key custody:

Draft answer (short): Default: Redwood-managed KMS with CMEK option for Dedicated/Private customers. For pilot customers we can propose a Bring-Your-Own-KMS model (customer keys in supported cloud KMS). Attached is a KMS custody summary (kms-attestation-summary.txt) and the recommended DPA annex wording to offer BYOK for key material.

> - Subprocessor roster and cross-border transfers:

Draft answer (short): Primary subprocessors: CDN provider (US), observability provider (US), long-term archive (US). No production inference or storage happens outside the US for this pilot unless customer explicitly opts into multi-region. For transfers we rely on SCCs where applicable; legal to confirm jurisdictional specifics.

Attachments to include when we reply to Medix: ingest-dataflow-v3.drawio (diagram), manifest-csv (table exported), kms-attestation-summary.txt. I've placed the diagram in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ingest-diagrams.

Jordan
Staff Solutions Engineer

PS: Kimberly — can you flag any non-US subprocessors if present? Vivek — can you draft the one-paragraph KMS custody attestation we can attach to the SSQ?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers and attachments below; please see the attached evidence pack and the diagram link. Happy to walk through this on a quick call — are you available Tue (10/7) morning PST?

Summary (high level)
- Ingest boundary & PII: Attached manifest enumerates fields we typically observe and flags those we classify as PII per your definition. Redwood classifies email, phone, national identifiers, and any health-identifying text as PII by default.
- Telemetry segmentation & retention: Content and telemetry are separated at the ingress proxy. Retention tiers we propose for the pilot: ephemeral debug logs (7 days), anonymized traces and sampling (90 days), aggregated analytics (3 years). Customers can opt out of non-essential telemetry.
- KMS custody: We offer Redwood-managed KMS by default and a BYOK option for Dedicated/Private customers. Attached is a short KMS custody attestation and BYOK instructions.
- Subprocessors & transfers: Current subprocessors involved in ingest and telemetry are listed in the attached roster. No inference or primary storage happens outside the US for the pilot; transfers are covered by SCCs where necessary.

Attached evidence pack (zipped PDFs): redwood-ssq-answers-medix-20251004.pdf (answers mapped to your SSQ), ingest-dataflow-v3.drawio (diagram), kms-attestation-summary.txt, subprocessor-roster-20251004.csv.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the manifest fields and retention tiers meet Medix requirements.
2) If you want BYOK for the pilot, we can schedule a short technical call to validate key provisioning.
3) We will share an updated DPA annex redline (legal) once technical details are finalized — HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/00000047.

If Tue morning works, I'll book 30 minutes and share an agenda. Thanks — looking forward to getting Medix over the finish line.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
